title: Poland’s cultural spending rose while physical and paid-digital access remained sharply stratified
source_unit: Statistics Poland, Participation in culture in 2024
geography: Poland; household cultural expenditure and residents aged 15 and over, by urban-rural residence, age, sex, and education

observations.period: 2024; household cultural expenditure and financial constraints

denominator.unit: households completing the April 2025 modular Participation in culture survey; expenditure measures come from the linked 2024 Household Budget Survey

annual_cultural_expenditure_per_member.unit: PLN per household member per year

cultural_expenditure_budget_share.unit: percent of total household expenditure, versus 2.0% in 2023

cinema_theatre_concert_entry_fees_urban.unit: PLN per urban household member per year

cinema_theatre_concert_entry_fees_rural.unit: PLN per rural household member per year

urban_rural_entry_fee_gap.unit: PLN per household member difference in annual entry-fee spending

financial_capacity_worsened.unit: approximate percent of households reporting worsened or considerably worsened ability to meet cultural needs

mechanism.value: Cultural spending can rise in nominal terms while affordability remains selective: entry-fee spending is much higher in urban households and cinema is the most common cultural activity abandoned for financial reasons

observations.method: Descriptive extraction from Statistics Poland's 2024 Participation in culture publication; expenditure measures come from the linked household-budget system and financial-abandonment measures from the household module.
observations.uncertainty: Cultural expenditure includes a broad recreation/sports/culture classification and is not a pure culture measure; nominal growth is not inflation-adjusted, and the survey does not establish whether urban-rural spending gaps arise from price, supply, income, travel, household composition, or preference.
observations.subgroup: Polish households, with urban-rural and socio-economic comparisons; expenditure generalized from the linked household budget survey.
observations.counterinterpretation: Higher urban entry-fee spending may reflect greater venue supply or different household composition rather than greater cultural desire; reported financial abandonment may also reflect prioritization, health, time, or access constraints.

observations.period: 2024; physical cinema attendance, paid online film access, and Internet use for cultural purposes

denominator.unit: households and household members aged 15 and over in the linked modular culture survey; published percentages are calibrated population estimates

cinema_attendance.unit: percent of people aged 15 and over declaring cinema attendance

paid_online_film_access.unit: percent using paid online film access, streaming, or VOD outside television/cinema

mechanism.value: Paid digital film access expands cultural consumption alongside cinema, but both channels retain strong urban-rural gradients and streaming has an extreme age gradient; digitization changes the channel without equalizing access

observations.method: Descriptive extraction from Statistics Poland's 2024 Participation in culture publication; physical attendance, paid film access, and cultural Internet-use shares are published subgroup estimates.
observations.uncertainty: The measures are annual-recall self-reports and do not establish subscription intensity, household sharing, price burden, content type, frequency, or whether streaming substitutes for or complements cinema attendance.
observations.subgroup: Polish residents aged 15 and over, by place of residence and age group.
observations.counterinterpretation: Urban and age differences may reflect broadband, income, education, household composition, language, content preferences, and venue proximity; paid streaming use does not establish cultural quality or participation depth.

related_sources.claim: Official Statistics Poland 117-page publication containing the English executive summary, tables, expenditure definitions, survey method, sample, calibration, and limitations.
Statistics Poland publication page describing the five-year modular survey, household expenditure, digital transformation, cross-sections, and downloadable PDF/XLSX tables.

boundary: This record adds a Polish cultural-consumption, affordability, physical/digital channel, and urban-rural/age stratification layer. It does not establish causal price effects, household welfare, cultural taste, substitution between cinema and streaming, or pure culture expenditure separate from recreation and sports.

reproduction_audit.retrieval_hash_scope: Statistics Poland publication page and English PDF reviewed; household expenditure, entry-fee urban-rural values, financial abandonment, cinema attendance, paid online film access, age/place gradients, sample, linked household-budget design, calibration, and category caveats checked.
